newsitem.title: UK: UK parliament security tightened amid IRA fears.
newsitem.headline: UK parliament security tightened amid IRA fears.

text.p: The British parliament tightened security on Monday amid fears that Irish Republican Army (IRA) guerrillas were planning a bomb attack before a general election due in the next few months.

"The Palace of Westminster (parliament building) remains at a high level of threat from the Provisional IRA," parliament's security chief Peter Jennings told the 4,000 staff working in the lower and upper houses.

"The IRA will be keen to gather whatever targeting information it can, especially concerning our security measures, including closed circuit TV coverage, access arrangements and patrols," he said in a letter quoted by The Times newspaper.
Access restrictions have now been imposed, passholders face random checks and bag searches are being intensified.

Security chiefs cited by the Times said IRA guerrillas had been carrying out covert surveillance operations in preparation for a bomb attack before the election, which Prime Minister John Major has to call by May.
The Irish National Liberation Army, an IRA splinter group, struck shortly before the 1979 election, killing Airey Neave, of a close ally of Margaret Thatcher, who became prime minister.
Neave's car was blown up by a bomb as he drove it out of parliament's underground car park.

The IRA, battling to oust Britain from Northern Ireland, ended a 17-month truce last February with a bomb attack in London that killed two people. It has also stepped up attacks on British troops and police in Northern Ireland.
